title: I will allure her (Hosea 2)
hookLine: God as a hurt husband who leads his people into the wilderness to speak to her heart

cards: Hosea's message came to him as a marriage. The book dates him by the kings he lived under, among them Jeroboam of Israel, and it opens with God telling him to marry a woman who would be unfaithful to him.
Her name was Gomer. They had three children, and each got a name that was a sermon. A son called Jezrahel, after a valley of bloodshed.
A daughter called Without mercy. A son called Not my people. Every time he called them in for dinner, he said a prophecy out loud.

teach.h: A CHARGE LIKE A DIVORCE COURT.
teach.b: Chapter two sounds like a divorce court. The husband is God, the wife is the people, and the charge is that she ran after other lovers, the Baals, the local gods, and gave them the credit for her grain and wine and oil.
The anger is real, and it goes on for verses. Then: therefore.
And in the Douay-Rheims: "Therefore, behold I will allure her, and will lead her into the wilderness: and I will speak to her heart." Not punish her. Allure her.
Win her back. The wilderness isn't exile; it's where the love story began, when God led the people out of Egypt and they were young.

teach.h: SPEAK TO HER HEART: SPEAK TENDERLY.
teach.b: Speak to her heart is a Hebrew phrase for speaking tenderly, the way you talk to someone you've hurt, or who has hurt you.
Joseph speaks to his brothers' hearts when he forgives them in Genesis; Isaiah is told to speak to the heart of Jerusalem.
By the end of the chapter, God promises: I will espouse thee to me for ever, in justice and mercy and faithfulness. The children's names are reversed. Without mercy will be shown mercy.

teach.h: NOT MY PEOPLE BECOMES MY PEOPLE.
teach.b: Not my people will hear: thou art my people.

teach.h: I WILL SPEAK TO HER HEART.
teach.b: Some Catholic writers have read Hosea alongside the Song of Songs, as God's love for his people and for each soul.

Some readers today find the picture hard, the wife cast as the one at fault and the anger so fierce, and they wrestle with that honestly. Either way, the turn is in the text: after all of it, therefore, tenderness.

how: Catholics hear Hosea's promise to speak to the heart in the Mass readings, and Catholic retreats sometimes take it up, describing days of silence as being led into the wilderness to listen.

o: a prophet who preached in the north

s: after the anger, God plans to lead his people into the wilderness to punish them
to allure her, and speak to her heart. the wilderness is where it began.
Hosea's children were given names that were messages
Jezrahel, Without mercy, and Not my people; the names are reversed by the end of chapter two.
speak to the heart is a Hebrew phrase found elsewhere in the Bible
Joseph speaks to his brothers' hearts, and Isaiah is told to speak to the heart of Jerusalem.

games.q: you're the hurt husband in Hosea's story. she ran after other lovers and forgot who loved her. the verse begins: therefore. what comes next?
o: therefore I will shut the door for good.
therefore I will allure her, lead her into the wilderness, and speak to her heart.
therefore I will send her away with nothing.
games.why: the word you'd expect to bring the punishment brings tenderness instead: I will allure her, and speak to her heart.

practice: Think of the last time you got something wrong, and the voice that started up afterward: a judge, a sigh, a list. Now picture the voice Hosea describes, the one that says therefore and turns gentle, leading you somewhere quiet.
If you pray, let God speak to your heart; if you don't, speak to yourself the way you'd speak to a friend.

wordCard.voice: Gomer. Hosea's unfaithful wife, whose story became God's promise to lead his people into the wilderness and win them back with tenderness. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: heart, the center of thought and will as well as feeling. to speak 'upon the heart' is to speak tenderly.

carryVoice: Your line: speak to her heart. Not my people becomes my people. That's four hundred twenty-six.

sources.ref: Hosea 2:14 (Osee 2:14 in the Douay-Rheims; 2:16 in the Hebrew numbering)
